NNEW CONCEPT ENGLISHBOOK 01 / 新概念英语

BOOK ONE · LESSON 134

He said (that) he… He told me (that) he…

他曾说他…… 他曾告诉我说他……

A picture lesson on reported speech: 'He said (that) he…' and 'He told me (that) he…'. Twelve pictures in four groups of three show direct speech being converted to reported speech (tired / reading / dinner / homework), illustrating the backshift of tenses (present → past, present perfect → past perfect). The lesson introduces written exercises A (answer questions about the Lesson 133 conversation using reported speech), B (answer 'What did he/she say?' with 'He/She said (that)…'), C (answer 'What did he/she tell you?' with 'He/She told me (that)…'), and D (answer with past perfect). The workbook drills reported-speech completion for a Ben Gold interview and open-ended situation questions; the grammar workbook rewrites sentences with 'said'/'told', completes a reported-speech dialogue, and writes short reports from given facts.

READ & UNDERSTAND

Lesson 课文

Listen and answer the questions.

听录音并回答问题。

I'm tired.

What did he say? What did he tell you?

He said (that) he was tired. He told me (that) he was tired.

I'm reading.

What did she say? What did she tell you?

She said (that) she was reading. She told me (that) she was reading.

We want our dinner.

What did they say? What did they tell you?

They said (that) they wanted their dinner. They told me (that) they wanted their dinner.

I've finished my homework.

What did he say? What did he tell you?

He said (that) he had finished his homework. He told me (that) he had finished his homework.

Practice A: He said that… and He told me that…

Look at the table. Then read the interview and write a simple report of what Ben Gold said to you. 看下表，阅读采访，根据 Ben 的回答写出一个简短的报道。

看下表，阅读采访，根据 Ben 的回答写出一个简短的报道。

6 reported-speech fill-in items; item 1 (Ben told me (that) he was 35 this year and (that) he still worked hard.) is the printed example. The table shows: 'I am right.' → he was right; 'I am driving carefully.' → he was driving carefully; 'I feel ill.' → he felt ill; 'I have read the newspaper.' → he had read the newspaper. The dialogue is an interview with pop star Ben Gold.
